layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, extracting the microvascular network, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: includes arterioles, venules, and capillaries, is challenging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to the limited contrast and resolution. As a result,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the vascular network often appears as fragmented seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments. In this paper, we propose a backbone-agnostic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Masked Vascular Structure Segmentation and Comple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion (MaskVSC) method to reconstruct the retinal vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network. MaskVSC simulates missing sections of blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels and uses this simulation to train the model to predict

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the missing parts and their connections. This approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simulates highly heterogeneous forms of vessel breaks and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mitigates the need for massive data labeling. Accordingly,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we introduce a connectivity loss function that penalizes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interruptions in the vascular network. Our findings show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that masking 40% of the segments yields optimal per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance in reconstructing the interconnected vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network. We test our method on three different types of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal images across five separate datasets. The results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrate that MaskVSC outperforms state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods in maintaining vascular network completeness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, MaskVSC has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been introduced to different segmentation backbones and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has successfully improved performance. The code and

layout_dets.text: I. INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RT m i e   y-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enter and exit the retina through the optic nerve head,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forming a unique closed loop system. The structure of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vasculature is dense, planar, and plexus-based. There are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 distinct plexuses: the superficial plexus which has a tree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, the intermediate and the deep plexus both have a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mesh structure. These plexuses are interconnected by verti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cal anastomoses. Parameters of the retinal angioarchitecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are indicators of retinal health, and are essential for under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standing the intricate perfusion of the eye. These parameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include the vessel diameter, localized dilatation or constriction,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stenosis, or occlusion, and the presence of neovasculariza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and/or leakage. Alterations in the angioarchitecture can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be associated with various physiological disorders, includ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing glaucoma [2], diabetic retinopathy (DR) [3], retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vein occlusion [4], and age-related macular degeneration [5].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiple imaging modalities map the continuous, intercon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nected retinal vascular network into the imaging domain,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capturing heterogeneous aspects of the retinal vasculature,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as illustrated in Fig. 1. For instance, snapshot fundus images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: primarily capture large vessels, and provide color information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about the veins and arteries. Other methods, such as single-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or two-photon fluorescence microscopy (2PFM) and optical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) [6], can image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumetric angiographic images, with capillary detail. Several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets have been released for fundus vessel segmentation [7],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [8], [9], [10] and artery-vein segmentation [11], [12], [13],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [14], [15], providing essential benchmarks for developing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robust segmentation methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accurate segmentation of vascular structures is crucial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the quantitative analysis of vasculature-related diseases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Key characteristics of the vascular segmentation task include

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handling of multi-scale, multi-orientation tubular structures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with crossings and branches. Traditional methods for vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation primarily involve designing filters that match the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tubular structure of the vessels [16], [17], [18]. Morphological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operations are also widely used [19], [20], [21]. However, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural elements defined by morphological operations are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assumed to be linear, which limits their effectiveness when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dealing with twisted and blurred vessels. Vessel tracking meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods [22], [23], [24] trace the segments between two selected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seed points for a single vessel to discover the best-matched

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: path, but they cannot detect vessels without seed points. Multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale methods [25], [26], [27], [28], [29] detect blood vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of different thicknesses by altering the image size or changing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the filter size. Machine learning algorithms [30], [31], [32],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [33], [34], [35], such as support vector machines and adaptive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boosting, can automatically detect retinal vessels, but they are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unlearnable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, these traditional methods require handcrafted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features, which limits their generalization and accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Over the last decade, deep learning (DL)-based methods have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emerged as powerful tools for vascular segmentation [36].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly useful for this task [37], [38], [39], [40], [41],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capturing multi-scale vascular information [42] through a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coarse-to-fine segmentation sequence [43] or by empha-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sizing fine spatial information [44]. Techniques such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundary detection [45] and edge enhancement [46] have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also been effective for fine vessel segmentation. The appli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation of the attention mechanism [47], which captures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global associations, has led to the development of vari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ous attention modules for retinal vessel segmentation with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: notable success [48], [49]. Additionally, Graph Neural Net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works (GNNs) [50], [51], which construct vessels into a graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, are well-suited for processing curvilinear structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data like angiograms [52], [53], [54].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite the good segmentation performance achieved by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods mentioned above, there are still several challenges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remaining:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Manually labeling vessels in retinal images is a cum-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bersome and time-consuming task, particularly for ine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and tiny vessels in images with a low signal-to-noise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ratio (SNR). This limits the amount of labeled data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) The topological integrity of the angioarchitecure is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impacted by disconnected and fragmented vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures, especially in small vessels or capillaries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address the challenge of limited data, the use of masking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or deletion is becoming increasingly popular. He et al. [55]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed an efficient self-supervised learning method called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Masked Autoencoder (MAE), which enhances the feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning ability and generalization performance of models by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: randomly masking input images to generate diverse train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing samples. Inspired by the above aspects of the work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a novel backbone-agnostic Masked Vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Structure Segmentation and Completion (MaskVSC) method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for predicting interconnected vascular structures with lim-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ited manually labeled data. Our main contributions are as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a comprehensive topology-aware mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (TopoMask) strategy by masking random portions of ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sel segments to simulate breakpoints or missing branches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in angiograms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a new connectivity loss function that guides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model to predict the same number of connectivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components as the ground truth, thereby penalizing vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fragmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Our MaskVSC method outperforms other state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology-based methods in preserving a more complete

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vascular structure across five different datasets containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three retinal imaging modalities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: II. RELATED WORKS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Curvilinear Structures Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Curvilinear structures, defined as elongated and line-like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formations, encompass a variety of natural and man-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made structures, including blood vessels. Given the similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges these structures face, even in varied con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: texts, solutions for their analysis often employ analogous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods [56].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON MEDICAL IMAGING, VOL. 44, NO. 6, JUNE 2025

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Methods for segmenting curvilinear structures can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: broadly categorized according to their prediction approaches:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Pixel/voxel-based methods [57], [58], which utilize local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or global information to compute a feature vector for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel/voxel, and then label each one based solely on its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features. 2) Edge-based methods [59], which estimate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positions of the curve's borders and subsequently fill the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interior region. 3) Shape-based methods [60], [61], which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rely on predefined templates and make predictions based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the similarity between the input and these templates.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4) Region-based methods [62], which extract the entire region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of interest and may involve post-processing steps to refine the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. 5) User-assisted methods [63], which require

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: varying levels of user involvement, from selecting seed points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to providing ongoing feedback throughout the segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process. 6) DL-based methods, which leverage labeled data to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predict segmentation on unseen samples through learning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DL-based methods can be further subdivided into: multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale [64], multi-task [65], [66], and attention mechanism-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based [67], [68]. The performance of these methods is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often constrained by the quantity and quality of available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations. To mitigate this limitation, several advanced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning methods based on weakly supervised [69], semi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised [70], self-supervised [71], and unsupervised [72]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning have been proposed. While these methods reduce the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependence on large labeled datasets, they often require com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex parameter selection tailored to different modalities. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adds an additional layer of complexity to their implementation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Topology-Based Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The curvilinear or tree-like structure of the vessels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the superficial plexus of the retinal vasculature serves as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior knowledge to design topology-aware loss functions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Improved performances have been achieved using an unsuper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vised vascular segmentation loss based on active contours [73]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a total variation regularization loss [74]. Shit et al. [75]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced a loss termed centerline Dice (clDice) that com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putes the intersection of segmentation and its morphological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: skeleton. Hu et al. [76] designed a continuous-valued loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (TopoLoss) that enforces the segmentation to have the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Betti number as the ground truth, where the Betti number

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is a topological invariant for characterizing connectivity and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of disconnected components. Further, they proposed a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss based on discrete Morse Theory (DMT) [77] to iden-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tify global structures for better topological accuracy [78].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Later, they used DMT and persistent homology to construct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a one-parameter family of structures as the topological rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resentation space [79]. Stucki et al. [80] introduced a Betti

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Matching error as a topological metric and loss, utiliz-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing induced matchings from persistent homology for spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matching of topological features. Gupta et al. [81] proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a topological interaction module to encode this constraint

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into end-to-end training. They further focused on uncertainty

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimation for identifying highly uncertain and error-prone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel structures [82].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. Post-Processing for Vessel Completion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To better preserve vessel continuity, several post-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing techniques have been developed, including:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully-connected Conditional Random Field (CRF) [83], local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gradient consistency extrapolation [84], [85], morphological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operation [7], [86], or a probability regularized walk [87].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Additionally, CRF models [88] are often employed in post-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing to enhance segmentation performance. Neverthe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less, traditional post-processing modules are unlearnable and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be challenging to optimize. Some studies have attempted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to integrate DL-based models [89], [90], [91], however,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic segmentation models do not necessarily preserve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the vascular topology. Several methods used synthetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disconnected vessel to train a reconnection model for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancing vascular connectivity after segmentation [92], [93],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whereas our MaskVSC integrates connectivity preservation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directly into the segmentation model by simulating missing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel segments and applying a connectivity loss.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: III. METHOD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we introduce MaskVSC - a backbone-agnostic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method for retinal vascular structure segmentation and com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pletion. It consists of three key components: a topology-aware

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask strategy TopoMask, a novel connectivity loss, and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Vision GNN (ViG)-based [94] post-processing. TopoMask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: randomly masks vessel segments, enabling the model to learn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: how to reconstruct these masked segments. Segment masking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simulates the vessel breakpoints that may appear in real

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal images. The ratio of masked breakpoints is adjusted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during training, allowing the model to learn generalized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representations of the vessels. The connectivity loss is pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed to enhance vascular continuity by penalizing fragmented

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segments. Subsequently, a ViG-based model post-processes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the initial prediction, leveraging the topological information of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal vessels by representing the image as a graph structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and processing the nodes and edges using graph convolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The training process has two steps. First, we train a vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation and completion model using TopoMask. Second,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we freeze its parameters and proceed to train a ViG-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model to refine the topology of the segmented vessels. During

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the testing phase, the raw retinal image is fed sequentially into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the vessel segmentation and completion model and then the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViG-based model to produce the final predicted vessel map.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The flowchart of MaskVSC is shown in Fig. 2, where (a) rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resents the first step of vessel segmentation and completion,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (b) represents the second step of post-processing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Topology-Aware Mask Strategy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inspired by the masking concept of MAE [55], we initially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimented with using MAE directly as a pre-training step

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for our task. However, this approach resulted in unsatisfactory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outcomes, particularly in maintaining vascular connectivity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is crucial for accurate vessel segmentation. This discrep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ancy may stem from the difference between the target of MAE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and our task. Natural images involve complex backgrounds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and overlapping objects, emphasizing overall category con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistency. In contrast, retinal blood vessels require continuity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and topology preservation, necessitating the accurate capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of fine vessels amidst noise and artifacts to maintain network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integrity and connectivity. Additionally, MAE is designed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large-scale natural image datasets, typically comprising tens

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of thousands of images. In the field of medical imaging, data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scarcity is a common challenge, leading to potential overfitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and low generalization. To address these challenges and better

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: imaging modality. This approach can prevent possible gradient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it, the model learns to handle incomplete data effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Connectivity Loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The vascular network of the retina is a fully interconnected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, making a fully-interconnected vascular representa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion essential. While several of the works introduced above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have focused on vascular connectivity, these topology- or post-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing-based methods typically emphasize either topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preservation or pixel-level connectivity. They often overlook

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the prior knowledge that an ideal prediction of vascular struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture should contain as few isolated components as possible.

layout_dets.text: C. ViG-Based Post-Processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: After the initial prediction from TopoMask, we utilize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the ViG [94] to post-process for better topological feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preservation. ViG treats an image as a graph by dividing it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into patches, each treated as a node, and constructs edges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by linking nodes according to K-nearest neighbors based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Euclidean distance. Retinal blood vessels have a sparse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure with an emphasis on connectivity, which is intuitively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better modeled by a graph rather than a mesh or normal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolution. ViG considers a vascular image as a graph and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processes it based on the connectivity between the nodes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This graph structure enables the model to capture spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relationships between patches, which is especially useful for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintaining connectivity in vascular structures. We choose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViG due to its ability to encode spatial dependencies and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuity patterns, which are essential for our tasks.

layout_dets.text: V. CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose a backbone-agnostic vascu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar structure segmentation and completion method called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MaskVSC. Our method includes a topology-aware mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategy (TopoMask) that simulates vessel breakpoints in reti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nal images. Additionally, a connectivity loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guides the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation of a more connected prediction, and ViG-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: post-processing further reduces false positives from TopoMask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by performing graphical structural analysis to refine the vas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cular structure. We conduct comparison experiments on five

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets containing three modalities, and MaskVSC achieves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: superior segmentation performance and topology preservation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to other state-of-the-art methods. This method has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential applications in other domains for extracting more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuous and interconnected linear or curvilinear structures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facilitating further studies on microvascular topology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lastly, we also notice several aspects that need improve-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment. First, despite our comprehensive evaluation, the data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tested in this study may not fully capture the diversity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diseases. Second, our approach is designed for 2D retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels, but vascular structures are inherently 3D. Developing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a framework capable of segmenting and complementing 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vascular structures is an important direction for future work.
